title: Un-Straightening Generative AI: How Queer Artists Surface and Challenge the Normativity of Generative AI Models

bias_targets.target: Sexual orientation and gender identity bias
bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative analysis of workshop discussions and prompt logs from queer artists, combined with a unigram logistic regression analysis of DALL-E 3's moderation system to identify the over-censorship of queer identities, sexuality, and intimacy, as well as the stereotyping of queer representation.

Qualitative evaluation by artists attempting to generate asymmetrical, glitchy, or non-normative artistic styles, observing the models' forced alignment to symmetry, high-fidelity realism, and toxic positivity.

Analyzing prompt rejection rates and model outputs for politically charged prompts, specifically critiques of law enforcement (e.g., 'ACAB'), using qualitative user testing logs and logistic regression of moderation features.

Qualitative observation of implicit biases in generated images, noting default whiteness in queer representation, 'copaganda' through forced diversity, and orientalist or geographically stereotypical tropes in art styles.

Analyzing the disproportionate censorship of female bodies and female-related prompts by image generation safety filters through qualitative participant experiences and unigram logistic regression showing the word 'female' highly associated with rejected prompts.

primary_bias_target: Sexual orientation and gender identity bias
